title_vi: Bản sao đọc: vì sao vừa ghi xong lại đọc không thấy

source_snapshot.note: Pinned commit/path body read from a partial clone of the source repository; git hash-object of the retrieved body matches the source-map blob. No source-image bytes used.

related.reason_vi: Bài cùng chủ đề trong nhóm, đi vào cách dựng mô hình bản sao đọc.
Độ trễ sao chép là một dạng nhất quán sau cùng.

claims.evidence: PostgreSQL 16 config.sgml (recovery_min_apply_delay, synchronous_commit) and high-availability.sgml (hot standby, synchronous standby planning, LSN monitoring) and the PostgreSQL 19 high-availability.sgml read-your-writes section were read from a partial clone of postgres/postgres; the lag and remote_apply measurements come from the author's own run on PostgreSQL 16.15 (two clusters on one machine) on 2026-10-18.

mobile.evidence: Chromium (Playwright) rendered lesson.md (markdown-it, tables enabled, every <details> open, a 16 px page gutter) at each width: the page never scrolled sideways and the figure was scaled to the column; the smallest SVG font-size times that scale is the recorded minimum at 320 px. `python3 -m scripts.figures check --browser` measured every line of the figure in Chromium inside its box. Not GitHub, not a real phone and not learner testing.

claims.claim_vi: recovery_min_apply_delay makes a standby replay each transaction commit only when its clock is at least the given delay past the commit time on the primary; only commit records are delayed.
claims.verified_by: Read from a partial clone of postgres/postgres at REL_16_STABLE commit 8e928803020e5b5694cde58e4851fce64ef9d520.

claims.claim_vi: With synchronous standbys configured, synchronous_commit=on waits until the standby has received and flushed the commit record; remote_apply waits until it has also applied it so it is visible to queries on the standby, which causes much larger commit delays.
claims.verified_by: Read from a partial clone of postgres/postgres at REL_16_STABLE commit 8e928803020e5b5694cde58e4851fce64ef9d520.

claims.claim_vi: synchronous_commit can be changed at any time and the setting in effect when a transaction commits decides its behaviour, so some transactions can commit synchronously and others not, e.g. with SET LOCAL inside one transaction.
claims.verified_by: Read from a partial clone of postgres/postgres at REL_16_STABLE commit 8e928803020e5b5694cde58e4851fce64ef9d520.

claims.claim_vi: Hot standby connections are strictly read-only; commits that wait for synchronous standbys may never complete if one of them crashes, unless several potential synchronous standbys are named; lag can be monitored by comparing pg_current_wal_lsn with sent_lsn of pg_stat_replication and pg_last_wal_receive_lsn with pg_last_wal_replay_lsn.
claims.section: Planning for High Availability; Hot Standby User's Overview; monitoring
claims.verified_by: Read from a partial clone of postgres/postgres at REL_16_STABLE commit 8e928803020e5b5694cde58e4851fce64ef9d520.

claims.claim_vi: PostgreSQL 19 documents read-your-writes consistency: after the write commits, take pg_current_wal_insert_lsn() on the primary and run WAIT FOR LSN on the standby before reading; the REL_16_STABLE docs have neither the section nor the command.
claims.verified_by: Read from a partial clone of postgres/postgres at REL_19_STABLE commit 10a0dcfc25fba51b2e0d3bbcb11584ecfb70f848; doc/src/sgml/ref/wait.sgml exists there and not at the REL_16_STABLE commit.

claims.claim_vi: Measured on PostgreSQL 16.15 with recovery_min_apply_delay=3s: right after commit the primary's insert LSN was 0/3027DD0 while the standby had replayed to 0/3027DA8 and returned 0 rows; polling until the replay LSN reached it took 2.9 s, then 1 row. With the standby synchronous, synchronous_commit=on returned in 0.0 s with the row not yet visible on the standby; remote_apply took 3.0 s and the row was visible right after. INSERT on the standby failed with 'cannot execute INSERT in a read-only transaction'.
claims.verified_by: The author ran and measured this on 2026-10-18 (pg_basebackup -R, streaming replication, two clusters on one machine); not repeated on other hardware.

claims.claim_vi: Read replica pattern: writes go to the primary and reads to replicas; replication lag can hide a just-written order; mitigations are routing latency-sensitive or read-after-write reads to the primary, or checking whether the replica has caught up.

design_notes_vi: Ba khung: đường đi của ghi và đọc, trình tự đọc ngay sau khi ghi lấy từ thử nghiệm, và ba cách sửa. Không dùng ảnh nguồn; ví dụ đơn hàng là của thử nghiệm riêng.
source_deviations: The source describes the check that a replica has caught up in general terms; the lesson makes it concrete with PostgreSQL LSN functions and measures it.
The lesson adds synchronous_commit=remote_apply as a third option with its cost, and notes (as the author's reasoning) that reads spread over two replicas can go backwards.
